name: Number Detectives
lesson: A factor divides a whole number with no remainder. A prime number has exactly two positive factors: 1 and itself. The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.
Common multiples help with repeating events. Common factors help when dividing different collections into identical groups without leftovers.
A number is divisible by 3 or 9 when its digit sum is divisible by 3 or 9. It is divisible by 4 when the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

problems.q: List all the prime numbers strictly between 10 and 20.
problems.hint: Exclude even numbers and multiples of 3 or 5.
problems.solution: The four remaining numbers are 11, 13, 17 and 19. Each has only 1 and itself as positive factors.

problems.q: List all the positive factors of 24.
What is the least positive number divisible by both 6 and 8?
problems.hint: Compare the multiples of 6 with the multiples of 8.
problems.solution: The first common positive multiple is $24=4\times6=3\times8$.

problems.q: There are 36 red counters and 48 green counters. They are put into as many identical bags as possible, with no counters left over. How many bags are made?
problems.hint: The number of bags must divide both quantities.
problems.solution: The greatest common factor of 36 and 48 is 12. Each bag then contains 3 red and 4 green counters.
The digit sum is $6+\square$. The only multiple of 9 from 6 to 15 is 9, so the missing digit is 3.

problems.q: Write 72 as a product of prime powers.
problems.hint: Repeatedly divide by the smallest prime factor.

problems.q: How many positive factors does 36 have?
problems.hint: List them in pairs, counting the square root only once.
problems.solution: The factors are $1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36$, for a total of 9.

problems.q: One bell rings every 8 minutes and another every 12 minutes. Both ring at 9:00. At what time will they next ring together?
problems.solution: The least common multiple of 8 and 12 is 24, so they next ring together 24 minutes after 9:00.

problems.q: What is the smallest whole number greater than 50 that is divisible by both 6 and 9?
problems.hint: Such a number must be a multiple of 18.
problems.solution: The common multiples are $18,36,54,72,\ldots$. The first greater than 50 is 54.

problems.q: Which digits can replace the square so that $5\square4$ is divisible by both 3 and 4?
problems.hint: Apply the digit-sum test and the last-two-digits test.
problems.solution: Divisibility by 3 allows digits $0,3,6,9$. Divisibility by 4 requires an even tens digit here. Their intersection is $0,6$.

problems.q: How many integers from 1 to 100 are divisible by exactly one of 2 and 5?
problems.hint: Numbers divisible by both must be excluded from each count.
problems.solution: There are 50 multiples of 2, 20 of 5 and 10 of both. Exactly one gives $(50-10)+(20-10)=50$.

problems.q: A rectangle has area $60\text{ cm}^{2}$ and positive whole-number side lengths. What is its smallest possible perimeter?
problems.solution: The pairs are $(1,60),(2,30),(3,20),(4,15),(5,12),(6,10)$. The pair $(6,10)$ has the smallest sum, giving perimeter $2(6+10)=32$ cm.
